ffuf -w /opt/SecLists/Discovery/DNS/subdomains-top1million-5000.txt:FUZZ \
     -u "http://FUZZ.academy.htb:PORT/"

# VHost fuzzing
ffuf -w /opt/SecLists/Discovery/DNS/subdomains-top1million-5000.txt:FUZZ \
     -u "http://academy.htb:PORT/" \
     -H "Host: FUZZ.academy.htb" \
     -fs <default_size>



ffuf -w /opt/SecLists/Discovery/Web-Content/web-extensions.txt:FUZZ \
     -u "http://subdomain.academy.htb:PORT/indexFUZZ" \
     -mc 200



ffuf -w /opt/SecLists/Discovery/Web-Content/DirBuster-2007_directory-list-2.3-small.txt:FUZZ \
     -u "http://subdomain.academy.htb:PORT/FUZZ" \
     -recursion -recursion-depth 1 \
     -e .php,.php7,.phps \
     -fs <empty_size> \
     -t 80



ffuf -w /opt/SecLists/Discovery/Web-Content/burp-parameter-names.txt:FUZZ \
     -u "http://subdomain.academy.htb:PORT/page.php7" \
     -X POST \
     -d "FUZZ=key" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
     -fs <default_size>



ffuf -w /opt/SecLists/Usernames/xato-net-10-million-usernames.txt:FUZZ \
     -u "http://subdomain.academy.htb:PORT/page.php7" \
     -X POST \
     -d "username=FUZZ" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
     -fs <default_size>












Tarea
Comando Base




Subdomain
ffuf -w dns.txt:FUZZ -u http://FUZZ.domain/


VHost
ffuf -w dns.txt:FUZZ -u http://domain/ -H "Host: FUZZ.domain"


Extension
ffuf -w ext.txt:FUZZ -u http://domain/indexFUZZ


Directory
ffuf -w dirs.txt:FUZZ -u http://domain/FUZZ


Page
ffuf -w pages.txt:FUZZ -u http://domain/FUZZ.php


Recursive
ffuf -w dirs.txt:FUZZ -u http://domain/FUZZ -recursion -e .php


Parameter GET
ffuf -w params.txt:FUZZ -u "http://domain/page?FUZZ=val"


Parameter POST
ffuf -w params.txt:FUZZ -u http://domain/page -X POST -d "FUZZ=val"


Value
ffuf -w values.txt:FUZZ -u "http://domain/page?param=FUZZ"
















Proposito
Wordlist




Subdomains
/opt/SecLists/Discovery/DNS/subdomains-top1million-5000.txt


Extensions
/opt/SecLists/Discovery/Web-Content/web-extensions.txt


Directories/Pages
/opt/SecLists/Discovery/Web-Content/DirBuster-2007_directory-list-2.3-small.txt


Parameters
/opt/SecLists/Discovery/Web-Content/burp-parameter-names.txt


Usernames
/opt/SecLists/Usernames/xato-net-10-million-usernames.txt







No agregar subdominios a /etc/hosts - Necesario para acceder a VHosts
Usar wordlist incorrecta - raft-* y common.txt no funcionan para recursive fuzzing
No filtrar por tamano - -fs es critico para limpiar resultados
Olvidar el header Content-Type - Requerido para POST en PHP
Formato incorrecto en respuesta - Usar “PORT” en lugar del numero de puerto

   ↓

   ↓
7. Value fuzzing en parametros encontrados

Descripcion

title: User Creation with Custom UID
text:
You just started as a Junior System Administrator at xFusionCorp Industries. On your first day, the Lead SysAdmin assigns you a task:

“The web development team needs a user named javed to deploy their application on server stapp02. They need UID 1467 and the home directory must be at /var/www/javed. The lead developer is waiting. Can you do it?”





Before creating users, you must understand how Linux manages them internally.


Every user in Linux is defined by a line in /etc/passwd:
username:password:UID:GID:comment:home_directory:shell
Example:
javed:x:1467:1467::/var/www/javed:/bin/bash

Key Insight: The UID is the user’s true identifier. Linux doesn’t say “user javed accessed”; it says “UID 1467 accessed”. Names are just human labels.




In large organizations, UIDs are assigned by ranges:

0-99: System users (root, bin, daemon)
100-999: Service accounts (nginx, mysql, docker)
1000+: Regular human users
10000+: Specific applications








# Connect via SSH
ssh steve@172.16.238.11

# Escalate to root
sudo su -



Always verify the current state before making changes:
# Check if user already exists
id javed

# Check if UID 1467 is already in use
grep "1467" /etc/passwd

# Verify /var/www/ exists
ls -ld /var/www/



useradd -u 1467 -d /var/www/javed -m javed
Command breakdown:



Option
Meaning
Why We Use It




-u 1467
Specify UID
Development team requirement


-d /var/www/javed
Custom home
Web application standard


-m
Create home directory
User needs a workspace


javed
Username
Human identifier






passwd javed

Security Best Practice: In production, configure SSH key authentication and disable password login: passwd -l javed




# Verify user exists with correct UID
id javed
# Expected: uid=1467(javed) gid=1467(javed) groups=1467(javed)

# Verify home directory
ls -la /var/www/javed

# Verify we can switch to user
su - javed
pwd  # Should show: /var/www/javed






User exists in /etc/passwd
UID is exactly 1467
GID matches UID
Home directory exists at /var/www/javed
Permissions are javed:javed
Configuration files copied (bashrc, etc.)
Can execute su - javed without errors





Explore variations of useradd:
# Service account (no login)
useradd -r -s /sbin/nologin mysql

# Add to secondary groups
useradd -G developers,deployers -m javed

# Account with expiration date
useradd -e 2025-12-31 -m contractor1





man useradd - Complete command documentation
man usermod - User modification
/etc/passwd format - Understanding the 7 fields





COMPLETED 🎉

Date: 2026-01-25
Time: 10-15 minutes
Level: Linux Administration Fundamentals
Skills: User Management, SSH, Verification

title: Non-Interactive Shell Users
text:
Company: xFusionCorp Industries
Project: Nautilus Automated Backup System
Task: Create a service account for automated backup processes




Service accounts are system accounts used by processes and services, not human users. They should never have interactive shell access.



Security: Prevents unauthorized access
Compliance: Follows least privilege principle
Automation: Works with cron, systemd services







User Type
Shell
Login Allowed




Human
/bin/bash
Yes


Service
/sbin/nologin or /usr/sbin/nologin
No










# Create user with non-interactive shell
useradd -s /sbin/nologin -M john

# Verify
id john
# Expected: uid=1001(john) gid=1001(john) groups=1001(john) shell=/sbin/nologin



# Attempting to login should fail
su - john
# Should show: This account is not available






User created with UID
Shell is /sbin/nologin
Home directory created or absent as needed
Login attempt denied

title: Group Management
text:
Company: xFusionCorp Industries
Project: Nautilus - Infrastructure Monitoring Platform
Location: Stratos Datacenter
Your Role: Senior System Administrator


The Network Operations Center (NOC) team is growing. A new monitoring engineer, Rajesh, needs consistent access to all Nautilus application servers.
The Challenge: Current servers don’t have standardized access management: - Security inconsistencies - Audit difficulties - Operational problems



Implement a standardized nautilus_noc group on 3 App servers and ensure Rajesh has consistent access through group membership.






Server
IP
Access User
Password
Purpose




stapp01
172.16.238.10
tony
Ir0nM@n
Nautilus App 1


stapp02
172.16.238.11
steve
Am3ric@
Nautilus App 2


stapp03
172.16.238.12
banner
BigGr33n
Nautilus App 3










Imagine you have 50 servers and 20 NOC engineers. Managing permissions user-by-user would mean 1,000 individual configurations. Groups reduce this to 50 group configurations + 20 membership assignments.



/etc/group       # Group definitions and members
/etc/gshadow     # Group passwords (rarely used)
/etc/passwd      # User info (includes primary group)
/etc/login.defs  # Default group configuration











Type
Purpose
Example




Primary
User’s default group
rajesh:x:1001:rajesh


Secondary
Additional access groups
nautilus_noc:x:1002:rajesh


System
Used by system processes
wheel, ssh, mail










# Connect to each server
ssh tony@172.16.238.10
sudo su -

# Check if nautilus_noc group exists
getent group nautilus_noc

# Check if user rajesh exists
id rajesh

title: Docker Installation
text:
Company: Stratos Datacenter
Role: Platform Engineer
Task: Install and configure Docker on stapp01 for the development team




Docker standardizes application packaging:

Package: Your app + dependencies
Standardize: Docker image format
Isolate: From the host system
Transport: Easily between environments


Platform Engineer Insight: Docker enables: - Microservices architecture - Fast CI/CD pipelines - Horizontal scaling - Cloud portability







ssh tony@172.16.238.10
sudo su -



# Update package index
apt-get update

# Install dependencies
apt-get install -y apt-transport-https ca-certificates curl gnupg lsb-release

# Add Docker GPG key
curl -fsSL https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu/gpg | gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/docker-archive-keyring.gpg

# Add Docker repository
echo "deb [arch=amd64 signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/docker-archive-keyring.gpg] https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu $(lsb_release -cs) stable" | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/docker.list > /dev/null

# Install Docker
apt-get update
apt-get install -y docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io



# Enable and start Docker
systemctl enable docker
systemctl start docker

# Add user to docker group
usermod -aG docker tony

# Verify installation
docker --version
docker run hello-world






Docker daemon is running: systemctl status docker
Docker version displayed: docker --version
Hello-world container runs: docker run hello-world
User can run Docker without sudo (after logout/login)
